rv.q: Mosaic deserves credit for championing new work.
Overall, this is a production with some very thought-provoking and poignant moments.

Precarious ends on a profoundly hopeful note for Tillie and Vi’s relationship, while still honoring the twinkling melancholy that suggests: If we truly want the world to be a better place for the generations to come, something has to give.
Schraf ensures we're engaged, at least, and considering the woman's humanity fully, regardless of how one might respond to, or question, her fanatical devotion to cleaning up the environment.

It was director Jaki Bradley’s staging of this moment, consistent with the rest of the production, with its focused, clear guidance of this comedic A-team cast (and the taught written script) that summoned our almost projectile laughter.
A fine, but uneven outing from Steph Del Rosso, which has a solid central performance but leaves a lot to be desired in the actual material.

cn.t: Critics praise *Precarious* for its timely exploration of climate anxiety and family disconnect, with strong performances—especially Kimberly Schraf—and sharp direction from Jaki Bradley earning consistent acclaim in this Mosaic Theater world premiere.
